title: US cotton export sales weaken on lower old crop bookings: USDA
content:
US cotton export sales weakened in the week ended July 30, with old crop cancellations and lower new crop bookings weighing on the report.
Upland sales fell to a marketing year low, while new crop bookings declined 31.3 per cent week on week.
However, continued forward buying from key markets including Vietnam, Turkiye, India and Pakistan provided underlying support to sentiment.

title: Under Armour is leaner and cheaper. Friday earnings prove if it works
content:
Under Armour is expected to post Q1 revenue of $1.11 billion and adjusted profit of $0.02 per share, with sales guided down 2-3 per cent.
Q4 inventories fell 3.3 per cent to $915 million, helped by disciplined buys, assortment rationalisation and a 25 per cent SKU cut.
North America turnaround, performance products and World Cup demand stay in focus, but promotions and tariff refunds remain.

title: ICE cotton rises further on high temperatures
content:
ICE cotton futures rose for the fifth time in six sessions, supported by persistent heat and dry conditions in major cotton producing regions, tight certified stocks, strong Chinese reserve demand, and supportive new crop export bookings.
The December 2026 contract settled at 83.16 cents, while longer dated contracts reached fresh contract highs, reinforcing the bullish market outlook.

title: Vietnam's sourcing edge faces a three-way cost squeeze
content:
Vietnam shipped textiles and clothing worth around $18.44 billion to the US in 2025, up roughly 13 per cent year on year.
A proposed 7.8 per cent regional minimum-wage rise from January 1, 2027 would set Region I at $217 per month.
A higher US tariff tier and exclusion from a US cotton-linked quota mechanism narrow Vietnam’s China-plus-one cost gap.

title: India's textile edge now hinges on capacity, not tariffs
content:
India’s textile industry has a once-in-a-decade sourcing opportunity, backed by tariff parity, a concluded EU trade agreement and policy support.
India sits in the 10 per cent tier of the new US Section 301 forced-labour tariff regime, but lacks TRQs and faces capacity execution risk.
Higher cotton MSP, viscose yarn duties and a 12.91 per cent October 2025 fall in exports to the US add pressure.

title: Vietnamese Resolution 10 shifts FDI strategy from attracting capital
content:
Vietnamese Politburo’s Resolution No. 10 is shifting the FDI strategy from attracting capital to enhancing investment quality; drawing high-value projects and advanced tech; and building stronger links between investors and domestic firms.
Its targets for 2025-2030 include attracting $200-300 billion in newly-registered FDI, disbursing $150-200 billion and integrating 10,000 firms into FDI supply chains.

title: Bangladesh RMG growth flips 23.4 points as US basics lose $250 mn
content:
Bangladesh's RMG growth swung from a 21.52 per cent rise in June to a 1.92 per cent fall in July, though earnings rose from June.
US imports from Bangladesh fell 8.08 per cent in January-May; EU imports dropped 18.89 per cent, with lower volumes and unit values.
TexPro says losses centred on men's woven garments and knitted T-shirts, which made up 87.6 per cent of the selected decline.

title: Energy, not tariffs, will decide Bangladesh’s export growth
content:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports were $3.89 billion in July 2026, down 1.92 per cent year on year but up 14.73 per cent from June.
US shipments rose 0.25 per cent to $918.74 million, and TexPro data show the market is stabilising.
A roughly 17 per cent gas-supply cut and 40-70 per cent capacity use are limiting factories despite a 10 per cent US tariff versus 12.5 per cent for Vietnam and China.

title: Can India's KKCL build on its 19% Q1 revenue growth?
content:
KKCL reported a strong Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations rising 19 per cent YoY to $29.14 million. 
EBITDA and PAT grew 29 per cent each, supported by volume expansion, a stronger brand portfolio, operational discipline and improved margins. 
The company remains confident of sustaining its growth momentum through FY27, backed by its integrated business model and continued focus on consumer demand.

title: Over 200 small Gazipur garment units declare 3-day break in Bangladesh
content:
Over 200 small and subcontracting garment factories in Bangladesh’s Gazipur declared a three-day break beginning today as low gas pressure, combined with the coming weekend, prompted managements to extend the break. 
Large mills and factories, however, will continue to operate at full capacity today. 
However, some major manufacturers have announced three-day breaks as well.
